column1: # DRAFT (not executed; see README.md). G1 phase 3: len and unique.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# len's argument is any integer-domain constraint (the count atom
# reuses the numeric algebra recursively); the domain — string length,
# list element count, map entry count — is fixed by the peer.
len-exact-list
len-window-list
len-reject-list
len-map
# String length is counted in UNICODE CODE POINTS — not UTF-16 code
# units (TS native) and not bytes (Go native). U+1D11E MUSICAL SYMBOL
# G CLEF is one code point, two UTF-16 units, four UTF-8 bytes.
len-string
len-string-codepoints
# len emptiness reuses the numeric algebra: len(c) empty iff
# c & integer & min(0) is.
len-empty
len-negative-empty
# unique() compares whole elements by scalar identity — leaf AND
# value — so [1, 1.0] IS pairwise distinct under the tower.
unique-ok
unique-reject
unique-leafwise
# DECIDED (see docs/reference-language.md, "`unique` semantics"):
# unique() applies to lists AND maps -- map ENTRY VALUES pairwise
# distinct, since keys are distinct by construction. Any other peer is
# a domain conflict. Uniqueness by PROJECTION ("no two services share a
# port") stays deferred to G8's combinators, arity reserved.
unique-map-ok
unique-map-reject
unique-string-domain
unique-scalar-domain
# Members compare by CANONICAL FORM, which reduces to scalar identity
# for scalars (unique-leafwise above) and gives structural equality for
# CONTAINER members without a second rule. Review caught that "scalar
# identity" alone left these undefined, which would have let the two
# ports pick different comparisons -- object identity in one, canon or
# generated value in the other.
unique-map-members-distinct
unique-map-members-same
unique-list-members-same
unique-nested-key-order
unique-map-of-containers
unique-mixed-shapes
# DECIDED (see docs/reference-language.md, "`len` semantics"):
# len counts what GENERATES. An optional key that never resolves is
# dropped at generation and does not count, so the first row HOLDS.
# len counts the members that WILL GENERATE, mirroring generation's own
# skip rules (type/hide marks, and an optional whose value cannot
# generate). That is knowable before generation runs: probing the engine
# shows a:{x:1,y?:number} converging DONE on the first pass with the
# optional child settled and simply not generable, so len decides
# eagerly there. It RESIDUATES only while an optional child is still
# converging (y?:$.z before z resolves), like any other deferring value.
# A supplied optional DOES count.
# Two earlier readings were wrong and are recorded so they are not
# re-invented: "residuates until the optional resolves or is dropped"
# (no such transition -- the drop happens only in BagVal.gen), and
# "completed at generation" (unnecessary -- the count is knowable
# earlier).
len-map-drops-unresolved-optional
len-map-counts-supplied-optional
len-map-optional-count-mismatch
# The residuation case: the optional child is still converging, so the
# count is not yet determined and len must defer rather than decide.
len-map-optional-resolves-late
len-map-optional-never-resolves
